text:
Jiayi Chen: onboarding veridian-v2 int4 — quick heads up: seen a drop in Cantonese named-entity transliteration quality and some weird RTL punctuation flips when Chinese + Arabic are mixed in the same sentence. Posting eval snippet below. Anyone seen this pattern with recent int4 kernels?

Amanda Lee: can you drop the eval numbers and which quant kernel you used?

Jiayi Chen: sure. ran with quant-kernel=ksv2-int4 (build abc123). benchmark: multilingual-translate-v0 (dev split). snippet: 
```
model: veridian-v2-int4
quant-kernel: ksv2-int4 (abc123)
benchmark: multilingual-translate-v0-dev
langs: zh-yue, zh-hant, ar->en, mixed-han-ar
BLEU: 
  zh-yue: baseline fp16=21.1 -> int4=15.4  (-5.7)
  zh-hant: baseline fp16=28.3 -> int4=26.9  (-1.4)
  ar->en: baseline fp16=34.2 -> int4=30.1  (-4.1)
mixed-han-ar punctuation mismatches: 7/120 examples (6%) show punctuation moved to the wrong side of Arabic spans
```

Tom Patel: yup that's alarming. do you have tokenization diffs for the failing Cantonese examples? could be subtoken merges after quantized kernel pruning.

Jiayi Chen: pasted small token-diff for one failing example: 
```
source: "港督同佢講咗關於香港特首林鄭月娥嘅事"
baseline tokens: ["港", "督", "同", "佢", "講", "咗", "關於", "香港", "特首", "林", "鄭", "月", "娥", "嘅", "事"]
int4 tokens:    ["港督", "同", "佢", "講咗", "關於", "香港特", "首林", "鄭月娥", "嘅事"]
note: matcher shows subtoken merges around named entity boundaries; decoder seems to hallucinate translit variants after merge
```

Sasha Ivanov: that token merge pattern looks like a tokenizer + text-normalization interaction. Could the int4 kernel be using a fused preproc path that accidentally applies legacy normalizer? run `token-diff --vocab veridian-v2 --mode compare --input sample.txt` and show token offsets.

Jiayi Chen: ran token-diff, offsets show changed split points (attached). Also saw the Arabic case: source: "قابلتُ 林 鄭، صباحاً" -> baseline preserves comma after Arabic token, int4 output becomes "قابلتُ 林 鄭 صباحاً،" (comma moved to end). Looks like punctuation attaching to RTL span on detokenization.

eval-bot: automatic note: reproduced 5/10 mixed-script failures on rerun with same build. Logs: https://internal-corp/evals/2412345678/logs

Amanda Lee: my guess: two orthogonal issues: 1) tokenizer normalization/merging changed token boundaries (affects CJK translit) 2) detokenizer bidi-handling path might be using a fallback that doesn't preserve punctuation side for Arabic when adjacent to fullwidth characters. Both could be triggered by kernel-level fused steps.

Tom Patel: plan: (1) bisect quant kernel variants: ksv2-int4 vs ksv1-int4 vs int4-stable (2) run tokenizer-only unit on same sample (3) add small mixed-script tests to premerge eval set and gate int4 rollouts

Sasha Ivanov: I'll take (2). Tom, can you bisect and ping deploy-bot when you have candidate kernels?

Tom Patel: starting bisect now. kicking off builds for ksv1-int4 and int4-stable, will run the multilingual-translate-v0-dev job. ETA ~40m. @deploy-bot can you watch the canary queue for these kernel names?

deploy-bot: watching canary queue for kernels: ksv1-int4, ksv2-int4, int4-stable. Will post status updates.

Jiayi Chen: added failing sample set + names to the repro gist: https://gist.internal/2412345678/cantonese-arabic-mix.txt

Amanda Lee: also check tokenizer vocab version bump in the build; earlier change https://repo/commit/0f9a2 touched token-normalizer and was rolled into ksv2-int4 build. If we revert normalizer change does that fix merges?

Sasha Ivanov: noted. I'll run tokenizer-only across the failing set with and without that normalizer flag.

Tom Patel: update: ksv1-int4 run finished. preliminary BLEU for zh-yue with ksv1-int4 = 20.8 (close to fp16). int4-stable still running. Looks like ksv2-int4 is the outlier.

Jiayi Chen: big relief if true. I'll hold rollout and add the mixed-script tests to the int4 gating job. Creating issue: https://issues.redwood/ENGML-987 (assigned to Tom)

Tom Patel: assigned ENGML-987 to self. will follow up with PR to pin tokenizer normalizer until we sort kernel changes.

Amanda Lee: thanks everyone. good triage. once we confirm kernel is culprit we can push a fix and re-evaluate. :thumbsup:

Jiayi Chen: thanks all — leave this thread open for updates, will post int4-stable results here.
